title: Chapter 59
content:
Emerging from the basement onto the ground floor, Jakyeong froze at the sight of Wang Han sitting in the living room.

How on earth did he track this place down?

Beside him sat Wang Ryun, hunched over with the posture of a condemned criminal. Judging by the miserable droop of his shoulders, Han had already torn him a new one.

Jakyeong padded over, testing the waters. Catching sight of them, Wang Han rose with a thunderous scowl, though his expression tightened into a disciplined mask the moment his eyes landed on Kang Il-hyun trailing behind.

Moving toward the foyer, the three operatives huddled together, slipping into rapid-fire Mandarin.

[What the hell is going on here? Since when is this Tokyo?!]

The moment Han had received the distress ping, shock and panic had sent him racing straight to Seoul on the first flight available. For all their talk about cutting losses if one of them was compromised, when the fire actually hit, the thought of his little brothers in a meat grinder had torn his insides to shreds.

[There were... extenuating circumstances,] Ryun muttered defensively.

[Circumstances?!] Han hissed. [I explicitly ordered you not to set foot anywhere near Korean airspace! And Wei—lying straight to my face about an undercover gig? You think that’s acceptable?]

[Ryun-ge got snatched because of me,] Jakyeong countered. [You expected me to just sit on my hands and watch?]

[So your grand rescue plan was getting yourself thrown into his basement dungeon?]

[Exactly,] Ryun chimed in, furrowing his brow. [The whole thing makes zero sense. Dropping your guard like an amateur—that's completely unlike you, Wei.]

[That psycho jammed a syringe into my neck before I could pull the trigger!]

[Narcotics?] Han’s eyes flared.

[A paralytic. The guy is an unhinged, sadistic bastard. I should have blown his brains out at the podium last year.]

[Preach,] Ryun nodded vigorously. [Total fucking scumbag.]

[Both of you, shut up!] Han snapped under his breath. [He's sitting right there!]

Wang Han was generally the most generous, easygoing man alive, but when his temper genuinely flared, he was terrifying. Knowing better than to poke the bear, Jakyeong and Ryun clamped their mouths shut, dutifully staring down at the tips of their shoes.

Lounging on the leather sofa, Kang Il-hyun watched the trio with deep amusement. He held an ice pack against his bruised jawline where Jakyeong had clocked him earlier.

If you’re going to conspire against me, at least take it out to the courtyard. Or did you honestly think I wouldn't understand Mandarin?

Thanks to their little huddle, he had received a crystal-clear refresher on just how much Lee Ja-kyeong despised his guts. Deciding the scolding had dragged on long enough, Il-hyun tapped his knuckles lightly against the glass coffee table: Tap, tap.

Three pairs of eyes snapped toward him in unison.

"I believe you've had sufficient time to catch up," Il-hyun said smoothly. "Shall we take our seats, gentlemen?"

The trio marched back to the living area, settling side-by-side on the sofa opposite him. Despite Il-hyun's polite tone, both Ryun and Jakyeong fixed him with identical, venomous glares.

Il-hyun set the ice pack down on the table. A dark purple bruise blossomed along his cheekbone, topped by a crust of dried blood at the corner of his lip. Jakyeong felt a quiet surge of petty triumph. When Ryun leaned in to whisper, asking if Jakyeong was the one who landed the punch, Jakyeong gave a subtle nod, earning a proud, gleeful grin from his older brother.

A maid brought out a tray of hot tea, followed by Park Tae-soo, who laid a leather-bound dossier before each of the three men.

Wang Han opened his folder first, followed by Ryun and Jakyeong.

It was an exclusive, high-level service retainer.

Without even reading past the first page, Wang Han snapped the folder shut, tossing it flat onto the glass. He had received a rough summary on the drive over, but the proposition was fundamentally absurd.

"My apologies, President Kang. We appreciate the consideration, but we must decline."

Ryun, casually thumbing through the financial appendices, nearly choked on his spit. The contract proposed a one-year exclusive retainer: the signing bonus, monthly executive stipends, and individual hazard pay per assignment totaled a dizzying, astronomical sum. His eyes bulging, Ryun aggressively nudged Jakyeong’s elbow, urging him to look at the figures.

Jakyeong glanced down at the numbers, then mirrored Wang Han—snapping the leather binder shut and tossing it aside.

Ryun hovered over the contract with lingering reluctance, only for Jakyeong to snatch the folder from his grip and toss it onto the pile.

"Are the terms not to your liking?" Il-hyun asked, tilting his head.

Wang Han kept his tone measured, careful not to provoke the predator. "We have received similar offers from various corporate syndicates over the years. However, we operate strictly as an independent unit. Being placed on a fixed leash under internal surveillance does not suit our methods."

Il-hyun offered an expectant look, silently inviting him to continue.

"Furthermore... given the rather unfortunate history between President Kang and our youngest, expecting seamless cooperation seems unrealistic, does it not? The foundation of trust is already fractured."

Il-hyun leaned back into the cushions, crossing his arms with a thoughtful hum.

An unfortunate history.

His dark eyes drifted across to Jakyeong. The kid was still glaring at him with a stubborn, defiant scowl. For someone who had supposedly spent the last four days on a hunger strike, he looked remarkably sharp. Then again, given the raw, explosive strength behind that right hook downstairs, the kid was clearly brimming with vitality. I was a fool for worrying and bringing dinner down myself.

"You need not concern yourself with that incident, Mr. Wang," Il-hyun replied casually. "I've already put it behind me. I am not the sort to hold petty grudges."

Seeing that the man had zero intention of backing down, Han fell quiet. On paper, the financial compensation was unprecedented, but working under a man who had already traded live fire with them was a lethal gamble.

Seeing the hesitation, Il-hyun nudged the contract back across the table toward Han.

"I invite you to remain as my guests for a few days to deliberate. Scrapping terms of this caliber over water under the bridge would be a terrible waste, wouldn't you say?"

The charming smile that followed made Jakyeong scowl deeper. Han cleared his throat, forcing an awkward, diplomatic chuckle. His primary objective was to extract his crew from this estate in one piece.

"President Kang may have moved past it... but our youngest clearly still harbors lingering resentment."

Hearing that, Il-hyun straightened his posture, fixing a warm, remarkably tender gaze on Jakyeong.

"What shall I do, then? Would you like me to apologize right here?"

Jakyeong shut him down instantly. "Save your breath."

Il-hyun’s brows drooped in mock sorrow. "I am truly, deeply sorry."

When Jakyeong answered with a derisive scoff, Il-hyun added smoothly:

"Next time we sleep together, I will be sure to obtain your explicit permission first."

Clatter.

The teacup slipped in Ryun’s grip, hot liquid splashing straight back into the porcelain saucer.

Wang Han’s jaw dropped so low it nearly hit his collarbone, his eyes widening in pure, disoriented shock.

Jakyeong froze, the breath trapped in his throat as he stared at Il-hyun in absolute, shell-shocked horror.

Il-hyun merely offered a casual, nonchalant shrug. "Did your brothers not know we shared that kind of intimacy?"

Unable to stomach another second, Han intervened, his voice tight with warning. "President Kang... that joke crosses a line."

Il-hyun let out a quiet, wicked chuckle. "Whether it's a joke or not... why don't you ask your darling little brother?"

Han and Ryun whipped their heads around in synchronized whiplash, their stares drilling straight into Jakyeong seated between them.

Jakyeong ground his molars together, glaring at Il-hyun with homicidal fury before turning frantically to his brothers with an incredulous, desperate scoff.

"You actually believe this lunatic?! It’s a complete lie!"

Both brothers wanted to brush it off as typical syndicate intimidation, yet the smug, unshakeable confidence radiating from Kang Il-hyun made doubt take root.

Thinking back on the past twelve months on the run, Jakyeong had maintained an eerie, absolute silence regarding his time in Seoul. Normally, an operative would brag about putting two rounds through a billionaire target over drinks, but Jakyeong had avoided the subject like the plague.

Could that be the reason...?

Under the suffocating weight of their stares, Jakyeong surged to his feet, knocking his knees against the low table.

"I'm not signing this goddamn paper! Hand over my gear—we're leaving!"

Fuming with rage, Jakyeong stormed out the double doors toward the gardens.

The moment Ryun moved to chase after him, Il-hyun smoothly rose to his feet, cutting him off.

"Rest easy, gentlemen. I'll go soothe him."

As Il-hyun vanished through the terrace doors, Wang Han and Wang Ryun stared at each other in dead, bewildered silence.

"Did he just say... soothe him?"

"Yeah. You heard that right."

Ryun looked down at the thick bandage swathing his reattached pinky finger. No wonder he rushed me into microsurgery the second I claimed to be his brother.

"Could it... actually be true?"

"Come on," Han muttered, trying to convince himself. "You know how much Wei loves pretty, delicate girls."

"Right... obviously."

Desperate to dispel the thought, both men turned their heads toward the panoramic garden windows.

Outside, Jakyeong was stomping across the lawn while Il-hyun caught him by the elbow. Jakyeong violently wrenched his arm free.

Under normal circumstances, Jakyeong would have met an adversary with cold, detached mockery or lethal precision; watching him throw a furious, emotionally raw temper tantrum was something neither brother had witnessed in a decade.

Outside, Jakyeong grabbed a stray wooden broom from the patio, snapped the head off with a vicious kick, and began swinging the splintered shaft like a combat staff.

Through the glass, Il-hyun looked like he was having the absolute time of his life.

Instead of worrying about a potential bloodbath, the entire display looked suspiciously like a pair of lovers having a passionate, domestic spat.

Han and Ryun broke their gaze from the glass, locking eyes once more.

Something is definitely wrong here.

Stomping across the manicured turf, Jakyeong felt a heavy hand clamp around his forearm.

He wrenched his arm back, pivoting on his heel to throw a vicious right cross. Il-hyun ducked the blow effortlessly. Losing his temper completely, Jakyeong snapped the handle of a nearby garden broom over his knee, whipping the heavy wooden pole toward Il-hyun's ribs.

Il-hyun sidestepped the arc, caught the wood mid-swing, and yanked it forward with concussive force.

Hauled off-balance, Jakyeong threw his head forward, attempting a brutal headbutt. Il-hyun slipped the strike by a hair's breadth—narrowly avoiding having his fractured jaw smashed open a second time—before clamping his hands down onto Jakyeong's shoulders in an iron grip.

"Darling... do you suffer from intermittent explosive disorder?"

"Funny," Jakyeong snarled through ground teeth. "I didn't think I did, but every time I look at your face, I'm overcome with a sudden urge to commit homicide."

As Jakyeong fought the hold, Il-hyun released his shoulders and reached into his tailored breast pocket. He withdrew a sleek leather cardholder, pinched a crisp, foil-embossed business card between two fingers, and presented it before Jakyeong’s eyes with radiant, boyish pride.

The embossed title read: President & CEO, Kang Il-hyun.

He waved the card teasingly before sliding it smoothly into the front pocket of Jakyeong’s shirt.

"I was promoted thanks to you. Belatedly... thank you."

As he slid the card in, his palm lingered, fingers subtly grazing over Jakyeong's chest. Jakyeong slapped the hand away with a sharp crack.

"Which brings me to my point," Il-hyun purred. "Lend me a hand just a little longer. I'll ensure your compensation is extraordinary."

"Why the hell would I ever trust you?"

"Don't trust me. Trust my money."

"..."

"I will pay the entire sum upfront in a single lump-sum transfer. Severance package included."

Jakyeong hesitated.

The signing bonus, the annual salary, and the full severance... all wired upfront in one shot?

He quickly tallied the figures from the contract in his head. Even split three ways, the payout was a colossal, life-altering fortune.

Seeing the subtle flicker in the boy's dark eyes, Il-hyun tilted his head, studying the shifting expression with a sly grin.

"The terms aren't bad, are they?"

Jakyeong bit down hard on his lower lip.

Meeting those conflicted dark irises, Kang Il-hyun couldn't resist letting a wicked, thoroughly depraved smirk curl across his lips.

"And if you'd like... you can have my cock thrown in as a signing bonus."
